spec.title: PROP-072: Source interpretation and boot observability

p.SOURCE-DESCRIPTOR-GRAMMAR: A package may declare sources in repeated `[[package.sources]]` TOML tables. Each row has exactly one selector, `file = "package-relative/path"` or `directory = "package-relative/path"`; `directory` is a default for descendants, not a glob, and neither selector may escape the package root or name a generated output. Each row requires `media`, `interpretation`, `role` and `loading` strings. The initial interpretation vocabulary is `vibe-spec`, `vibe-doc`, `commonmark`, `xml-data`, `opaque`; the role vocabulary is `spec`, `documentation`, `resource`; the loading vocabulary is `scan`, `explicit`. `scan` may enumerate a declared source of any interpretation, but only `vibe-spec` or `vibe-doc` may mint their respective Vibe facts or addresses. Ordinary CommonMark contributes structural navigation without Vibe facts; XML data and opaque resources remain data or raw bytes. `media` records the declared media type separately from interpretation; it must be a normalized nonempty media-type token and is checked against the selected reader before that reader runs. An unknown value or incompatible combination refuses rather than widening a parser. The descriptor's durable resource identity is the package coordinate plus its normalized relative file path, independent of filename suffix, target materialization format and current physical bytes. No table field grants trust: origin, selected declaration, captured source bytes, source hash, generated/authored status and verification are host-observed provenance, retained separately from authored intent.

p.SOURCE-DESCRIPTOR-PRECEDENCE: For one normalized file identity, an exact `file` row wins over every matching `directory` default. Otherwise the longest matching directory path wins; a directory matches only its own descendant components, not a textual prefix. Identical equally specific declarations may coalesce, but incompatible equally specific rows produce a path-specific `NeedsInput` outcome and confer no semantics. A selected declaration must still pass media/syntax validation. Extension, location, parsable XML, Markdown markers and successful syntax sniffing never create a missing Vibe declaration. A source with no proved interpretation remains raw and unclassified; a foreign bridge source defaults to no Vibe interpretation. In a `simple` package, literal `#use` and related directive-looking text remain literal package content; descriptor selection does not change the package-format and boot-link contracts.

p.SOURCE-MIGRATION-LAW: Source declaration migration extends the incumbent M-13 authored-manifest planner, exact replay, one-file application admission and recovery journal; it does not create another executor. Its source and target profiles, recipe and recognized old grammar are explicit, finite and revisioned. No package version, absent manifest epoch, suffix, directory convention or syntactically valid content selects a source interpretation. An old authoritative declaration may be translated only when its meaning maps uniquely; conflicting or unknown per-resource intent yields a typed, path-specific `NeedsInput` question and leaves the authored file unchanged. A successful plan retains exact before/after text, ordered edits and identities; insertion of new declaration rows is represented by validated zero-length edits, and multiple edits replay in source order. All untouched bytes, including comments, whitespace, quote style, existing field values and order, survive exactly. The current Manifest owner validates the complete result after the frozen profile check. If the edit span, question, profile or output cannot be proved, migration refuses; planning never writes, and application still requires the existing explicit ownership grant and recheck.

p.SOURCE-OBSERVATION-LAW: Every interpreted read, projection, conversion, scan and refusal identifies the normalized resource; it carries the selected descriptor and declaration origin when one exists, the captured byte identity when bytes were read, the reader/converter recipe when one ran, and whether positions refer to source or projection. A missing descriptor, unsupported media or vocabulary, ambiguous selection, invalid syntax and unavailable bytes remain distinct incomplete or unsupported observations; none is reported as an empty document or successful scan. Ordinary data remain retrievable as original bytes even when optional structure inspection fails. This contract extends PROP-045 `SOURCE-CLASSIFICATION-LAW`; it does not assert that existing scanners, resolvers, materializers, boot readers or migration surfaces already implement it.
